svg.title: The 2021 WHO CNS5 decision tree: three gates first, then the five-item list
svg.desc: Schematic decision tree for how the 2021 WHO CNS5 classification arrives at the name glioblastoma. Step one is three entry gates, all of which are required: adult-type (not a paediatric-type diffuse glioma), diffuse (not one of the circumscribed gliomas), and astrocytic glioma. Only once all three gates are passed does step two ask whether IDH (isocitrate dehydrogenase) is mutated. On the IDH-mutant side a second question follows, 1p/19q co-deletion: co-deleted gives oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted; not co-deleted gives astrocytoma, IDH-mutant, grade 2, 3 or 4, and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A/B makes it grade 4 outright without waiting for histology. The IDH-wildtype side goes to step three, a list of five criteria of which any single one is enough: microvascular proliferation, necrosis, TERT promoter mutation, EGFR amplification, and gain of whole chromosome 7 with loss of whole chromosome 10. Meeting one of them gives glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4. Three side notes sit off the main path: first, lack of an IDH mutation alone is not enough to call a tumour grade 4, because plenty of more indolent tumours are also IDH-wildtype, so one of the five criteria must still be met; second, EGFR must show focal high-level amplification, trisomy 7 does not count and immunohistochemistry cannot be used to call amplification; third, in a young patient think of paediatric-type diffuse glioma first, as CNS5 no longer applies the word glioblastoma to paediatric-type tumours. At the foot of the figure two proportion bars carry US registry data from CBTRUS 2018 to 2022: among all brain and other CNS tumours, glioblastoma is 13.7 per cent, meningioma 42.6 per cent and other tumours 43.7 per cent; among malignant tumours only, glioblastoma is 52.2 per cent and other malignant tumours 47.8 per cent. For Taiwan the figure states only that 742 new brain cancers were registered in 2023, with no official breakdown for the glioblastoma share. The figure contains no survival numbers.

g.text: 2021 WHO CNS5 — HOW THE NAME IS DECIDED
Three gates first, then the five-item list
The 2021 WHO CNS5 classification asks three entry questions first;
only once all three are passed do the molecular criteria count.
This figure shows how a name is reached. It carries no survival
numbers — those belong to the article on what the numbers mean.
Step 1 | Three gates (entry conditions, all three required)
Adult-type
not a paediatric-type diffuse glioma
Diffuse
not one of the circumscribed gliomas
Astrocytic glioma
a diffuse glioma of astrocytic lineage
Only after all three gates does the molecular work-up decide the name.
Step 2 | Is IDH (isocitrate dehydrogenase) mutated?
IDH-mutant
Ask once more: 1p/19q co-deletion?
Co-deleted
Oligodendroglioma, IDH-mutant and 1p/19q-codeleted
Not co-deleted
Astrocytoma, IDH-mutant (grade 2 / 3 / 4)
On the astrocytoma branch: homozygous deletion of CDKN2A/B makes it grade
4 outright, without waiting for histology.
IDH-wildtype (no IDH mutation)
Step 3 | Five criteria — any single one is enough
Microvascular proliferation
Necrosis
TERT promoter mutation
EGFR amplification
Gain of whole chromosome 7 and loss of whole chromosome 10 (+7 / −10)
Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4
Side notes (off the main path, and often got wrong)
Lack of an IDH mutation on its own is not enough to call something grade 4 —
plenty of more indolent tumours are also IDH-wildtype, so one of the five
criteria above still has to be met (cIMPACT-NOW update 3).
EGFR must show focal high-level amplification. Trisomy 7 does not count, and
immunohistochemistry cannot be used to call amplification (cIMPACT-NOW
update 3).
In a young patient, think of paediatric-type diffuse glioma first; CNS5 no
longer applies the word "glioblastoma" to paediatric-type tumours.
How much of all brain tumours it accounts for (US registry data, CBTRUS 2018–2022)
All brain and other CNS tumours
Meningioma 42.6%
Other 43.7%
Glioblastoma 13.7%｜Meningioma 42.6%｜Other 43.7%
Malignant tumours only
Glioblastoma 52.2%
Other malignant tumours 47.8%
Both bars are US registry data. For Taiwan: 742 new brain cancers were registered in
2023; what share of them were glioblastoma, I could not find an official breakdown for.
Schematic, redrawn from the 2021 WHO CNS5 classification (Louis 2021),
cIMPACT-NOW update 3 (Brat 2018) and CBTRUS 2018–2022; the cohorts,
designs and endpoints of the underlying studies differ, so the data points must
not be compared directly.
